how_to_read: Fields beyond id/title/source: `buzz` = how many DISTINCT outlets carry the same story (corroboration). `seen` = the paper already ran this story on that date: pick it again ONLY if there is a genuinely new fact (a verdict, number, reversal), never for continued interest. `flags` = why a desk editor would be wary (press-release wording, company's own channel, roundup/opinion format, weak fit with the section): treat flagged items as guilty until the text proves a real event. `when` (opportunities) = the real deadline/event date. stories.title: Satellites show some of the strongest evidence the AMOC is weakening
stories.summary: The crucial Atlantic current system that brings warmth to Europe has slowed 14 per cent in 30 years, according to an analysis of how much heat the ocean is releasing to the atmosphere
stories.extract:
Satellite measurements suggest the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) has been transporting less heat towards Europe, providing some of the strongest evidence yet of a slowdown in these ocean currents, which keep Europe’s climate mild.
The AMOC system of currents, which includes the Gulf Stream, brings warm, salty water from the Gulf of Mexico to the north Atlantic, where it cools and sinks, returning south along the sea floor.
